content.overview: Section 14 allows a company to alter its articles by special resolution, subject to the provisions of the Act and the conditions contained in the memorandum. Entrenchment provisions have additional requirements. A copy of the altered articles must be filed with the Registrar.
content.glance: State that articles may be altered by special resolution; note the limits of the Act and memorandum; mention entrenchment and filing.
content.study: Subject to the provisions of the Act and the conditions in the memorandum, a company may, by special resolution, alter its articles. The alteration is valid as if originally contained in the articles. Where the articles contain entrenchment provisions, those provisions may be amended only in the manner specified for entrenchment (typically a more stringent procedure). A copy of every special resolution altering the articles, and of the altered articles, must be filed with the Registrar. Articles cannot authorise what the Act forbids or contradict the memorandum. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in s. 14 and distinguish s. 13 (memorandum alteration).

sections.heading: Special Resolution
sections.body: Articles may be altered by special resolution of the company.

sections.heading: Limits — Act and Memorandum
sections.body: Alteration is subject to the Act and the conditions in the memorandum; articles cannot override either.

sections.heading: Entrenchment
sections.body: Entrenchment provisions require the more stringent procedure specified for their amendment.

sections.heading: Filing
sections.body: A copy of the special resolution and of the altered articles must be filed with the Registrar.

examples.title: Valid articles alteration
examples.body: A company passes a special resolution to change its board-meeting quorum rules in the articles and files the altered articles. Section 14 is complied with.

examples.title: Conflict with memorandum
examples.body: An altered article purports to expand objects beyond the memorandum. The alteration is ineffective to the extent of the conflict; s. 13 is the route for object change.

hypotheticals.question: Can articles be altered by board resolution alone?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 14 requires a special resolution of the company.

hypotheticals.question: Can an article override a memorandum clause?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Alteration under s. 14 is subject to the memorandum; conflict is resolved in favour of the memorandum.

distinctions.title: Alteration of articles (s. 14) vs memorandum (s. 13)
distinctions.left: Internal regulations; special resolution; subject to Act and memo
distinctions.right: Charter change; special resolution plus often CG/RD approval

misconceptions.trap: Articles can be freely rewritten without regard to the memorandum.
misconceptions.correction: Section 14 expressly subjects alteration to the Act and the memorandum.

misconceptions.trap: Entrenchment can be removed by ordinary special resolution without more.
misconceptions.correction: Entrenchment provisions may be amended only in the manner specified for entrenchment.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.
cases.relevance: Already in file; articles regulate the internal life of the incorporated person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 14 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm special resolution. II. Test against Act and memorandum. III. Check entrenchment if relevant. IV. Confirm filing. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Resolution status; conflict with Act/memo if any; entrenchment; filing; precise relief.

examTips: Always check Act and memorandum limits.
